checkpoints.name: top_is_alu
checkpoints.description: The top module NetCrux opens is `alu`, with the four ports the RTL declares.

checkpoints.name: output_is_a_mux
checkpoints.description: The output `y` is driven by a 2:1 multiplexer — the `op ? sum : a` selector. Students find the $mux cell in the alu module.

checkpoints.name: adder_is_a_submodule
checkpoints.description: Addition lives in its own block: `alu` instantiates `adder4`. Pushing into it in NetCrux reveals the $add cell.

checkpoints.name: adder_contains_the_add
checkpoints.description: Inside adder4, the arithmetic is a single $add cell over the 4-bit inputs.
